purpose: P1.5 MEDIUM tier data for activities/awards/research/course rigor/major selectivity (extensions to v2 §3.2)

confidenceTierDefinitions.HIGH: Official school publication (admissions blog / class profile / CDS)
confidenceTierDefinitions.MEDIUM: Crimson / IvyWise / industry expert aggregate / Common App reports

admitsWithResearchPct.source: Caltech publicly reports 45% of admitted Class of 2027 conducted research
Industry report: nearly one-third of UPenn Class of 2026 had research experience
Inferred — peer to Caltech (45%), STEM-heavy school

globalT20DefaultEcProfile.applicableTo: Top 20 schools without per-school EC data

admitsWithNationalAwardPct.source: Common App: 55%+ admitted students at selective institutions list state-level or higher honor
admitsWithNationalAwardPct.note: This includes state-level; pure national-level alone estimated ~30-40%

admitsAvgApCount.source: Spark Admissions / Crimson aggregate: Most Ivy admits complete 10-14 APs

admitsWithSpikePct.source: Counselor consensus / MIT Admissions FAQ: depth + sustained involvement over breadth
admitsWithSpikePct.note: No direct number published, estimate from qualitative emphasis on 'spike' at T20

admitsWithLeadershipPct.source: Counselor consensus; Common App leadership-section completion rates

admitsAvgActivityCount.source: Common App allows 10 activities; admits typically fill ~8
admitsAvgActivityCount.note: Inferred from Common App fill rates

globalT21_50DefaultEcProfile.applicableTo: Schools ranked 21-50, when no per-school data

majorSelectivityMultipliers.purpose: Per-school program-specific admit rate, expressed as multiplier vs overall

perSchool.source: Reports: Stanford CS admit rate ~1.8% vs overall 3.6-4%
MIT does not admit by major; 6-8% figure reflects intended-CS scrutiny, not actual major-based admit
CMU SCS widely understood to be much more selective than overall CMU

majorTierDefaults.comment: When per-school per-major data unavailable, use these tier defaults

highly_competitive_at_school.examples: CS at most T20, Business at Penn Wharton, Engineering at Cornell

uncompetitive_relative.examples: Humanities at STEM-focused schools, certain regional studies

essayQualityData.note: No public aggregate exists. Use existing essayQualityScore (0-10) from your AI essay review.

modifiers.comment: Treat as student-side signal vs implicit T20 threshold (admits assumed to clear essay screen)

knownGapsAndAcceptedLimitations: Per-school EC depth (% with spike) — only LOW tier global estimate, no per-school numbers published
Per-school activity counts — Common App doesn't break down by school
Award-level granularity — '55% with state+ honor' is overall; need finer breakdown by national vs intl
Major selectivity for non-CS programs — only CS collected; engineering / business / pre-med need separate research
Essay quality — no public data, rely on existing AI score
